newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba expects big gathering at trade fair despite U.S. law.
newsitem.headline: Cuba expects big gathering at trade fair despite U.S. law.

text.p: Cuba expects a bigger-than-ever turnout at its annual international trade fair next month, despite a seven-month-old U.S. law aimed at discouraging business with the island, authorities say.

Trade fair organiser Abraham Maciques told the Cuban business paper Opciones, published Tuesday, that about 1,600 foreign firms from 55 countries were expected to be represented at the fair in Havana on Nov. 3-10.
"This shows the confidence there is in Cuba," he added.

Newcomers to the fair include firms from South Korea, Indonesia, Monaco, Finland and Namibia, while the countries with the largest exhibition areas will be Spain, Italy, Panama and Canada -- reflecting their positions as key trading partners of Cuba.

The U.S. Helms-Burton law, aimed more at investors than traders, includes provisions to sue in U.S. courts foreign firms deemed to be doing business on property formerly owned by U.S. firms or individuals that was nationalised after Fidel Castro's 1959 revolution. The legislation has been widely criticised by Washington's allies.
Maciques said that while Helms-Burton was not aimed at trade, it could still discourage traders because of threats that businesses dealing with Cuba might receive.
